I'm skipping Enlgish class again just to write this. I seriously need help...

Thing is, my parents are stingy with money, so hiring a tutor seems kind of meh. They also think I'm this amazing young man who can do anything, but I'm just a lazyass. This is partially true... however... I think there is more than just wishing to go on the internet more often. I am seriously depressed and have anxiety problems, but they do not care - they continue to label me as lazy and don't listen to me.

In addition, I am beginning to hate my family... my parents are old-fashioned, uninterested, sloppy parents. My sister is better than that, but we had one of the worst fights in my entire life last night. I can't do this anymore... sometimes I just wish I could find a space in the stock room of a store and live there, just so I'll be alone. I could try and live with them longer in this house, that will allow me to save money, but we might be moving to Calgary if my dad gets accepted by the Hospital that interviewed him last week, so ehhh. Plus, this doesn't get rid of them, they will only continue to disrespect my independance like they've been doing increasingly since I've gotten older. I want to have to deal with my consequences rather than having them constantly ask me questions about every single goddamn thing in my life, the most prominent being homework. Hell, even things like putting on my shoes or grabbing my lunch are questioned. I'm not a damn 5 year old.

I understand they are apparently doing their job as parents, but they're never going to let me go at this rate... I don't have anyone to turn to.

fnck man, the story of the last year of my life.

I'm getting on track though. I had a fallout over summer where I would get on the forums and IRC instead of going to class. In the beginning of this Fall term I was getting on quite often, but I only had one class. My finals are tomorrow and it looks like I'll either get a low A or a high B.

The thing some people need is to hit rock bottom before they realize they are screwed. I was almost kicked out of my program (it lets me take college classes in return for high school credit and eventually a high school diploma) because of how often I was on here. I'm still on pretty often, just not as much as I used to be. I was seriously depressed for most of summer, and my mom has started to call me lazy and incompetent over the last 4 or so months. Almost every morning, too. Seems like I'm in the same boat you are, just a couple steps ahead in the "recovery" process.

One thing that you NEED to do is talk to a close friend about every fncking thing you have posted here. Doesn't matter if they can't help you. Sometimes letting your problems be known by more than just you and some random people you met online can help a lot. At the end of this last summer, me and a friend of mine had a long talk about another friend, but ended the whole 2 hour conversation with what scares us the most about growing up and what we thought of our family. For her, I think it helped just telling someone the most minute details of what she thought of our friend, and for me, I got the chance to finally tell someone why I disliked my mother so much, in a place between two people who weren't going to start laughing and brush off the conversation (this had happened a couple times before with another person).

If you think talking to people here is going to help you, it's not. Mostly because we don't know you. From what you posted I can identify readily, because I've been through what you posted. There may be more, so don't expect me to have been through everything you have. Just what you posted I identify with directly. This is why it is important to talk to a friend. Someone who knows you. Let them know beforehand that it is a serious conversation, and that you need to get some things off your chest. That way you don't just start up a serious conversation without the person being ready for it.

As for what Obby said, there is a lot of truth to that. And yeah, you'll probably get angry at him, but know that there is a difference between saying something and doing something. That's a lesson I had to learn, it's probably your time to learn it now.

The best of luck to you. I truly hope that you make something out of this and you can reflect on this experience and learn from it.

-southpaw-

#392805 47 2007-12-23T23:48:09Z southpaw
Obby:

The fact of the matter is that your God is unique in that no single person believes in exactly the same God you do. God, in all His glory, is subjective.

Therefore if God is subjective it is up to you to determine how your God acts within the realms of reality. If you pray to God hoping that refugees in Darfur will be saved then that is how you think your God should act. If a preacher tells you that God is all-loving and will send the righteous to Heaven, but that people who participate in abortions (who may have faith as well) are going to hell, it is up to you to decide whether your God would allow that to happen or not.

Since God is subjective, Pascal's Wager relies completely on if you think your God is going to send you to eternal suffering if you do not believe in him and follow the teachings of his Word in the Bible. If you believe that your God loves you and forgives you for your actions on Earth, even if what you did was morally "wrong," then what is the point of adopting Pascal's Wager as a basis for turning to religion? That was Pascal's God. Not mine or yours.

#397079 7 2008-01-05T04:43:38Z southpaw
Here are a couple things you can do (sorry if you already said you did them I was kinda confused reading through your first post):

1. Plug the speakers into your mp3 player to make sure that when plugged into another source they play in stereo. If they don't play in stereo still then it is a problem with the actual speakers and not your computer.

2. Check your volume settings. It may be that the balance for the Master volume got moved over to the right speaker. If that's the case just move the marker back into the middle.

3. If the above two are not the problem then it's probably something to do with your computer (either a setting or problem with the speaker jack itself). It seems that it may be the computer, seeing as how when you plug your headphones into the computer they don't play in stereo either.

That's all I can think of. Hope that helps.

Those who want to learn - Those who actually come to school to learn and get a good college education for a low price. 20% of the students (the percentage is from a report of the success of the program) are effectively either here to learn, or were here to learn but certain life issues had come up and they were no longer able to come to class or get the education they wanted.

Those who don't want to learn - Those who come to the program and either drop out in the first term or drop out in some term after. About the 10 Commandments:
What the 10 Commandments are to me is God's laws for Man, not for Himself. I would agree that a strong leadership requires a good role model ("If God kills people I can too!") but I stand by my thinking that God intended the 10 Commandments for Man and Man alone.

Quote: iangb, 2008-01-10T13:28:11Z
There's only one way to quote text, really, and that deals with the facts of the words, not the interpretation of them.
There is one way to quote text, but that doesn't mean there is only one way to interpret it. There is no single interpretation of a single passage. The facts of the words and the interpretation of the words are two different things.
Though I agree that this certain passage leaves very little room for interpretation, it is the interpretation of a passage that is more important when reading holy text than literal meaning, IMO.

Example:
It is a fact that the color "red" has a wavelength of ~625-740 nm. It is not a fact that red is love and warmth and passion, as well as anger and rage, or even a definition for the action to stop. Yet society as a whole interprets "red" as such, regardless of what it's true definition is. So to say that a passage is only interpretable in one way and that way is the facts of the words and the meaning of the words is absurd.

Quote: Ravenclaw, February 10, 2008 03:04 pm
Rap, to me, just sounds like black guys singing about shooting people, selling drugs, and beating women. I don't understand why it's so popular.
There are two main types of rap in my opinion:

1. Rappers who rap about shooting people, selling drugs and beating women, as well as personal things that happened to them to help a person understand what it is that they have gone through; and
2. Rappers who rap about shooting people, selling drugs and beating women because the other guys talk about it.

*NOTE: there is a third, which consists of those who mostly make music that doesn't tell a story, but isn't pointless either. Artists like Tech N9ne, De La Soul and Mac Dre seem to fit into this third category. The lyrics aren't exciting and the beat isn't superb but they work together and make a song that isn't annoying but isn't spectacular in any way.*

Rappers who fit into number 1 would be: Tupac, Eminem, Run DMC, Grandmaster Flash, Kanye West, Lil Wayne, Immortal Technique, etc.

Rappers who fit into number 2 would be: Vanilla Ice, Soulja Boy, Ja Rule, Fat Joe, Akon, Mike Jones, T-Pain, Three 6 Mafia, etc.


Rappers in number 2 may have gone through the same things as rappers in number 1 but they come of as rapping without a purpose, whereas rappers in number 1 are rapping because they have something to say and have a story to tell.



Even though you can't hear the lyrics and the emphasis, here are some lyrics of songs from rappers in number 1 compared to those in number 2:
-Number 1-
  • Stan by Eminem
  • Staring Through My Rear View by Tupac Shakur
  • Dance With The Devil by Immortal Technique (this song is probably the best. I hate putting only the lyrics up because it's much better when you listen to the song.)
---
-Number 2-
  • Make It Rain by Fat Joe
  • Lean Wit It by Dem Franchize Boyz
  • Put Ya Signs by Three 6 Mafia
Of course this has a lot of bias and some artists are based off of one or two songs (such as putting Grandmaster Flash into number 1 because of "The Message"), but I think it holds some merit. Personally what I find is that rappers in number 1 usually have less catchy beats which is why they are much more influential because they make up for it with lyrics that make sense and tell a story.

The moon turned its dark side to my eyes,

#19319 1 2008-02-26T01:57:59Z southpaw
A friend of mine showed me this the other day and I wanted to hear the community's thoughts on it. I found it immensely interesting and although I may not fully agree with the concept I found myself wondering about for most of today.

It is quite an outstanding read for this forum but I think a lot of you might find this interesting.

Quote: From "the Holographic Universe" by Michael Talbot
In 1982 a remarkable event took place. At the University of Paris a research team led by physicist Alain Aspect performed what may turn out to be one of the most important experiments of the 20th century. You did not hear about it on the evening news. In fact, unless you are in the habit of reading scientific journals you probably have never even heard Aspect's name, though there are some who believe his discovery may change the face of science.

Aspect and his team discovered that under certain circumstances subatomic particles such as electrons are able to instantaneously communicate with each other regardless of the distance separating them. It doesn't matter whether they are 10 feet or 10 billion miles apart.

Somehow each particle always seems to know what the other is doing. The problem with this feat is that it violates Einstein's long-held tenet that no communication can travel faster than the speed of light. Since traveling faster than the speed of light is tantamount to breaking the time barrier, this daunting prospect has caused some physicists to try to come up with elaborate ways to explain away Aspect's findings. But it has inspired others to offer even more radical explanations.

University of London physicist David Bohm, for example, believes Aspect's findings imply that objective reality does not exist, that despite its apparent solidity the universe is at heart a phantasm, a gigantic and splendidly detailed hologram.

To understand why Bohm makes this startling assertion, one must first understand a little about holograms. A hologram is a three- dimensional photograph made with the aid of a laser.

To make a hologram, the object to be photographed is first bathed in the light of a laser beam. Then a second laser beam is bounced off the reflected light of the first and the resulting interference pattern (the area where the two laser beams commingle) is captured on film.

When the film is developed, it looks like a meaningless swirl of light and dark lines. But as soon as the developed film is illuminated by another laser beam, a three-dimensional image of the original object appears.

The three-dimensionality of such images is not the only remarkable characteristic of holograms. If a hologram of a rose is cut in half and then illuminated by a laser, each half will still be found to contain the entire image of the rose.

Indeed, even if the halves are divided again, each snippet of film will always be found to contain a smaller but intact version of the original image. Unlike normal photographs, every part of a hologram contains all the information possessed by the whole.

The "whole in every part" nature of a hologram provides us with an entirely new way of understanding organization and order. For most of its history, Western science has labored under the bias that the best way to understand a physical phenomenon, whether a frog or an atom, is to dissect it and study its respective parts.

A hologram teaches us that some things in the universe may not lend themselves to this approach. If we try to take apart something constructed holographically, we will not get the pieces of which it is made, we will only get smaller wholes.

This insight suggested to Bohm another way of understanding Aspect's discovery. Bohm believes the reason subatomic particles are able to remain in contact with one another regardless of the distance separating them is not because they are sending some sort of mysterious signal back and forth, but because their separateness is an illusion. He argues that at some deeper level of reality such particles are not individual entities, but are actually extensions of the same fundamental something.

To enable people to better visualize what he means, Bohm offers the following illustration.

Imagine an aquarium containing a fish. Imagine also that you are unable to see the aquarium directly and your knowledge about it and what it contains comes from two television cameras, one directed at the aquarium's front and the other directed at its side.

As you stare at the two television monitors, you might assume that the fish on each of the screens are separate entities. After all, because the cameras are set at different angles, each of the images will be slightly different. But as you continue to watch the two fish, you will eventually become aware that there is a certain relationship between them.

When one turns, the other also makes a slightly different but corresponding turn; when one faces the front, the other always faces toward the side. If you remain unaware of the full scope of the situation, you might even conclude that the fish must be instantaneously communicating with one another, but this is clearly not the case.

This, says Bohm, is precisely what is going on between the subatomic particles in Aspect's experiment.

According to Bohm, the apparent faster-than-light connection between subatomic particles is really telling us that there is a deeper level of reality we are not privy to, a more complex dimension beyond our own that is analogous to the aquarium. And, he adds, we view objects such as subatomic particles as separate from one another because we are seeing only a portion of their reality.

Such particles are not separate "parts", but facets of a deeper and more underlying unity that is ultimately as holographic and indivisible as the previously mentioned rose. And since everything in physical reality is comprised of these "eidolons", the universe is itself a projection, a hologram.

In addition to its phantomlike nature, such a universe would possess other rather startling features. If the apparent separateness of subatomic particles is illusory, it means that at a deeper level of reality all things in the universe are infinitely interconnected.

The electrons in a carbon atom in the human brain are connected to the subatomic particles that comprise every salmon that swims, every heart that beats, and every star that shimmers in the sky.

Everything interpenetrates everything, and although human nature may seek to categorize and pigeonhole and subdivide, the various phenomena of the universe, all apportionments are of necessity artificial and all of nature is ultimately a seamless web.

In a holographic universe, even time and space could no longer be viewed as fundamentals. Because concepts such as location break down in a universe in which nothing is truly separate from anything else, time and three-dimensional space, like the images of the fish on the TV monitors, would also have to be viewed as projections of this deeper order.

At its deeper level reality is a sort of superhologram in which the past, present, and future all exist simultaneously. This suggests that given the proper tools it might even be possible to someday reach into the superholographic level of reality and pluck out scenes from the long-forgotten past.

What else the superhologram contains is an open-ended question. Allowing, for the sake of argument, that the superhologram is the matrix that has given birth to everything in our universe, at the very least it contains every subatomic particle that has been or will be -- every configuration of matter and energy that is possible, from snowflakes to quasars, from blu whales to gamma rays. It must be seen as a sort of cosmic storehouse of "All That Is."

Although Bohm concedes that we have no way of knowing what else might lie hidden in the superhologram, he does venture to say that we have no reason to assume it does not contain more. Or as he puts it, perhaps the superholographic level of reality is a "mere stage" beyond which lies "an infinity of further development".

Bohm is not the only researcher who has found evidence that the universe is a hologram. Working independently in the field of brain research, Standford neurophysiologist Karl Pribram has also become persuaded of the holographic nature of reality.

Pribram was drawn to the holographic model by the puzzle of how and where memories are stored in the brain. For decades numerous studies have shown that rather than being confined to a specific location, memories are dispersed throughout the brain.

In a series of landmark experiments in the 1920s, brain scientist Karl Lashley found that no matter what portion of a rat's brain he removed he was unable to eradicate its memory of how to perform complex tasks it had learned prior to surgery. The only problem was that no one was able to come up with a mechanism that might explain this curious "whole in every part" nature of memory storage.

Then in the 1960s Pribram encountered the concept of holography and realized he had found the explanation brain scientists had been looking for. Pribram believes memories are encoded not in neurons, or small groupings of neurons, but in patterns of nerve impulses that crisscross the entire brain in the same way that patterns of laser light interference crisscross the entire area of a piece of film containing a holographic image. In other words, Pribram believes the brain is itself a hologram.

Pribram's theory also explains how the human brain can store so many memories in so little space. It has been estimated that the human brain has the capacity to memorize something on the order of 10 billion bits of information during the average human lifetime (or roughly the same amount of information contained in five sets of the Encyclopaedia Britannica).

Similarly, it has been discovered that in addition to their other capabilities, holograms possess an astounding capacity for information storage--simply by changing the angle at which the two lasers strike a piece of photographic film, it is possible to record many different images on the same surface. It has been demonstrated that one cubic centimeter of film can hold as many as 10 billion bits of information.

Our uncanny ability to quickly retrieve whatever information we need from the enormous store of our memories becomes more understandable if the brain functions according to holographic principles. If a friend asks you to tell him what comes to mind when he says the word "zebra", you do not have to clumsily sort back through ome gigantic and cerebral alphabetic file to arrive at an answer. Instead, associations like "striped", "horselike", and "animal native to Africa" all pop into your head instantly.

Indeed, one of the most amazing things about the human thinking process is that every piece of information seems instantly cross- correlated with every other piece of information--another feature intrinsic to the hologram. Because every portion of a hologram is infinitely interconnected with ever other portion, it is perhaps nature's supreme example of a cross-correlated system.

The storage of memory is not the only neurophysiological puzzle that becomes more tractable in light of Pribram's holographic model of the brain. Another is how the brain is able to translate the avalanche of frequencies it receives via the senses (light frequencies, sound frequencies, and so on) into the concrete world of our perceptions. Encoding and decoding frequencies is precisely what a hologram does best. Just as a hologram functions as a sort of lens, a translating device able to convert an apparently meaningless blur of frequencies into a coherent image, Pribram believes the brain also comprises a lens and uses holographic principles to mathematically convert the frequencies it receives through he senses into the inner world of our perceptions.

An impressive body of evidence suggests that the brain uses holographic principles to perform its operations. Pribram's theory, in fact, has gained increasing support among neurophysiologists.

Argentinian-Italian researcher Hugo Zucarelli recently extended the holographic model into the world of acoustic phenomena. Puzzled by the fact that humans can locate the source of sounds without moving their heads, even if they only possess hearing in one ear, Zucarelli discovered that holographic principles can explain this ability.

Zucarelli has also developed the technology of holophonic sound, a recording technique able to reproduce acoustic situations with an almost uncanny realism.

Pribram's belief that our brains mathematically construct "hard" reality by relying on input from a frequency domain has also received a good deal of experimental support.

It has been found that each of our senses is sensitive to a much broader range of frequencies than was previously suspected.

Researchers have discovered, for instance, that our visual systems are sensitive to sound frequencies, that our sense of smell is in part dependent on what are now called "osmic frequencies", and that even the cells in our bodies are sensitive to a broad range of frequencies. Such findings suggest that it is only in the holographic domain of consciousness that such frequencies are sorted out and divided up into conventional perceptions.

But the most mind-boggling aspect of Pribram's holographic model of the brain is what happens when it is put together with Bohm's theory. For if the concreteness of the world is but a secondary reality and what is "there" is actually a holographic blur of frequencies, and if the brain is also a hologram and only selects some of the frequencies out of this blur and mathematically transforms them into sensory perceptions, what becomes of objective reality?

Put quite simply, it ceases to exist. As the religions of the East have long upheld, the material world is Maya, an illusion, and although we may think we are physical beings moving through a physical world, this too is an illusion.

We are really "receivers" floating through a kaleidoscopic sea of frequency, and what we extract from this sea and transmogrify into physical reality is but one channel from many extracted out of the superhologram.

This striking new picture of reality, the synthesis of Bohm and Pribram's views, has come to be called the holographic paradigm, and although many scientists have greeted it with skepticism, it has galvanized others. A small but growing group of researchers believe it may be the most accurate model of reality science has arrived at thus far. More than that, some believe it may solve some mysteries that have never before been explainable by science and even establish the paranormal as a part of nature.

Numerous researchers, including Bohm and Pribram, have noted that many para-psychological phenomena become much more understandable in terms of the holographic paradigm.

In a universe in which individual brains are actually indivisible portions of the greater hologram and everything is infinitely interconnected, telepathy may merely be the accessing of the holographic level.

It is obviously much easier to understand how information can travel from the mind of individual 'A' to that of individual 'B' at a far distance point and helps to understand a number of unsolved puzzles in psychology. In particular, Grof feels the holographic paradigm offers a model for understanding many of the baffling phenomena experienced by individuals during altered states of consciousness.

In the 1950s, while conducting research into the beliefs of LSD as a psychotherapeutic tool, Grof had one female patient who suddenly became convinced she had assumed the identity of a female of a species of prehistoric reptile. During the course of her hallucination, she not only gave a richly detailed description of what it felt like to be encapsuled in such a form, but noted that the portion of the male of the species's anatomy was a patch of colored scales on the side of its head.

What was startling to Grof was that although the woman had no prior knowledge about such things, a conversation with a zoologist later confirmed that in certain species of reptiles colored areas on the head do indeed play an important role as triggers of sexual arousal.

The woman's experience was not unique. During the course of his research, Grof encountered examples of patients regressing and identifying with virtually every species on the evolutionary tree (research findings which helped influence the man-into-ape scene in the movie Altered States). Moreover, he found that such experiences frequently contained obscure zoological details which turned out to be accurate.

Regressions into the animal kingdom were not the only puzzling psychological phenomena Grof encountered. He also had patients who appeared to tap into some sort of collective or racial unconscious. Individuals with little or no education suddenly gave detailed descriptions of Zoroastrian funerary practices and scenes from Hindu mythology. In other categories of experience, individuals gave persuasive accounts of out-of-body journeys, of precognitive glimpses of the future, of regressions into apparent past-life incarnations.

In later research, Grof found the same range of phenomena manifested in therapy sessions which did not involve the use of drugs. Because the common element in such experiences appeared to be the transcending of an individual's consciousness beyond the usual boundaries of ego and/or limitations of space and time, Grof called such manifestations "transpersonal experiences", and in the late '60s he helped found a branch of psychology called "transpersonal psychology" devoted entirely to their study.

Although Grof's newly founded Association of Transpersonal Psychology garnered a rapidly growing group of like-minded professionals and has become a respected branch of psychology, for years neither Grof or any of his colleagues were able to offer a mechanism for explaining the bizarre psychological phenomena they were witnessing. But that has changed with the advent of the holographic paradigm.

As Grof recently noted, if the mind is actually part of a continuum, a labyrinth that is connected not only to every other mind that exists or has existed, but to every atom, organism, and region in the vastness of space and time itself, the fact that it is able to occasionally make forays into the labyrinth and have transpersonal experiences no longer seems so strange.

The holographic prardigm also has implications for so-called hard sciences like biology. Keith Floyd, a psychologist at Virginia Intermont College, has pointed out that if the concreteness of reality is but a holographic illusion, it would no longer be true to say the brain produces consciousness. Rather, it is consciousness that creates the appearance of the brain -- as well as the body and everything else around us we interpret as physical.

Such a turnabout in the way we view biological structures has caused researchers to point out that medicine and our understanding of the healing process could also be transformed by the holographic paradigm. If the apparent physical structure of the body is but a holographic projection of consciousness, it becomes clear that each of us is much more responsible for our health than current medical wisdom allows. What we now view as miraculous remissions of disease may actually be due to changes in consciousness which in turn effect changes in the hologram of the body.

Similarly, controversial new healing techniques such as visualization may work so well because in the holographic domain of thought images are ultimately as real as "reality".

Even visions and experiences involving "non-ordinary" reality become explainable under the holographic paradigm. In his book "Gifts of Unknown Things," biologist Lyall Watson discribes his encounter with an Indonesian shaman woman who, by performing a ritual dance, was able to make an entire grove of trees instantly vanish into thin air. Watson relates that as he and another astonished onlooker continued to watch the woman, she caused the trees to reappear, then "click" off again and on again several times in succession.

Although current scientific understanding is incapable of explaining such events, experiences like this become more tenable if "hard" reality is only a holographic projection.

Perhaps we agree on what is "there" or "not there" because what we call consensus reality is formulated and ratified at the level of the human unconscious at which all minds are infinitely interconnected.

If this is true, it is the most profound implication of the holographic paradigm of all, for it means that experiences such as Watson's are not commonplace only because we have not programmed our minds with the beliefs that would make them so. In a holographic universe there are no limits to the extent to which we can alter the fabric of reality.

What we perceive as reality is only a canvas waiting for us to draw upon it any picture we want. Anything is possible, from bending spoons with the power of the mind to the phantasmagoric events experienced by Castaneda during his encounters with the Yaqui brujo don Juan, for magic is our birthright, no more or less miraculous than our ability to compute the reality we want when we are in our dreams.

Indeed, even our most fundamental notions about reality become suspect, for in a holographic universe, as Pribram has pointed out, even random events would have to be seen as based on holographic principles and therefore determined. Synchronicities or meaningful coincidences suddenly makes sense, and everything in reality would have to be seen as a metaphor, for even the most haphazard events would express some underlying symmetry.

Whether Bohm and Pribram's holographic paradigm becomes accepted in science or dies an ignoble death remains to be seen, but it is safe to say that it has already had an influence on the thinking of many scientists. And even if it is found that the holographic model does not provide the best explanation for the instantaneous communications that seem to be passing back and forth between subatomic particles, at the very least, as noted by Basil Hiley, a physicist at Birbeck College in London, Aspect's findings "indicate that we must be prepared to consider radically new views of reality".

#19428 1 2008-03-07T19:52:34Z southpaw
I have an idea that I think would be awesome to implement.

I was thinking back to when Arachnid asked for all the collaboration accounts on NUMA so that he could disable the voting priveleges on all of them. But wouldn't it be easier if you could just have the option to choose a collaboration option when submitting a map?

Here's how it would work:
  • When you are submitting a map there would be a checkbox above the Map Name section that you could select that said something like "collaboration?" or "Multiple authors?". Doing so would open up a single text box with an option to create more text boxes beside it.
  • In the text boxes would go the names of the author(s) that you collaborated with. This would then signify that you and the said author(s) created a map together and that you are submitting it to all the names. All names would also be verified so that you couldn't put in a name that didn't exist.
  • When the map is submitted and voting takes place on it the votes will go not only to the author that submitted it but also to the author(s) that were involved as well. For example, if Yahoozy_Guacamole and remote collaborated on a map and Yahoozy submitted it any votes that were placed would also count toward remote's average NUMA rating.
  • To prevent faulty ratings, and using the example above, if remote were to rate the map a 5 the rating would only go toward Yahoozy's NUMA rating and not remote's, in this way eliminating any ability for personal gain. Likewise, Yahoozy would be able to rate the map as well because his vote would only be counting toward remote's average NUMA rating.
I know that there are probably a few holes in this system. Fortunately that's where you, the community, come in. What do you think?

I gave the whole thing a three because I love the avatar, but I don't like the siggy. Here's a few suggestions:

I have judged every entry. I'll post up what I sent max_ride because either he didn't get it or he hasn't posted it yet:
Spoiler: Judging for people who think I didn't judge them Yahoozy_Guacamole - Axis II
Aesthetics: 3.5/5
Amount of fun: 8.5/10
How well you used the enemy: 6/10
---
Total: 18/25
---
This map played much better than I thought it would. The tileset wasn't spectacular but it worked well with the gameplay. I also liked the variation of adrenaline pumping sections and then cooldown areas. Good job.

Skyline356 - The Corbity Columns of Craining Callows
Aesthetics: 4.5/5
Amount of fun: 9/10
How well you used the enemy: 10/10
---
Total: 23.5/25
---
This was orgasmic. But not an orgasm. There's a difference.

Cerberus[] - Inevitable Shock
Aesthetics: 3.5/5
Amount of fun: 7/10
How well you used the enemy: 8/10
---
Total: 18.5/25
---
This map was nice but it just didn't really click well with me. I like the way you used the enemies and I liked the tileset and the way it worked with the gameplay but it seemed like it was missing something. The part I enjoyed the most was that it looks like a race map at first glance but then it becomes partially action as you play it.

Gforce - CEC 01
Aesthetics: 2/5
Amount of fun: 4/10
How well you used the enemy: 5/10
---
Total: 11/25
---
This didn't do it for me. The amount of time spent completing this map did not correlate with how much fun it was. AGD was long and tedious and boring. Unless there is a certain path that makes it not tedious and long and boring I found it so.

JackPack - 90 Degrees
Aesthetics: 1.5/5
Amount of fun: 4/10
How well you used the enemy: 5/10
---
Total: 10.5/25
---
I wasn't impressed by this at all.

Evil_Bob - Heart Attacks
Aesthetics: 3.5/5
Amount of fun: 7/10
How well you used the enemy: 9.8/10
---
Total: 20.3/25
---
Of course it's an Evil_Bob puzzle... Why did I try and think it was an action map? haha, I liked it. It was frustrating at first but after a few goes (and cheating only slightly) I figured out the path I needed to take. Very clever map.

Myrrhman - Guernika
Aesthetics: 4/5
Amount of fun: 7/10
How well you used the enemy: 8/10
---
Total: 19/25
---
I liked it.

Nexx - Nexx CE3 Entry
Aesthetics: 4/5
Amount of fun: 8/10
How well you used the enemy: 8/10
---
Total: 20/25
---
I liked this map a lot. The drones were put in all the right places and it wasn't just a clearcut route that one has to follow. There was some thinking involved, which is nice. Great job.

Hopefully that is everybody. If someone still hasn't had their map judged by me, PM me and I'll get on that right away.

#19567 1 2008-03-18T09:47:24Z southpaw
If any of you have ever been on deviantArt.com and have an account there then you will know what I am talking about straight off the bat.

For those of you who do not, I will explain what "Watching" is. When you create a deviantArt account and start to find artists that you like and think are really cool you have the option to "watch" them. Basically what Watching does is send you a notice that there are submissions you have not viewed that were posted by the people you have decided to Watch. This allows you to be up-to-date with what your favorite artists have done recently. It's a nice tool to have and I find it very handy because I don't have to check an artists page often to see if they've posted anything new. Instead I'll get a message telling me when they have posted something new.


I know there are a lot of authors out there that are well known. I know that the search function is very capable of getting you to the author you would like fairly quickly. I know some people have gone far enough to add their favorite authors to their webpage browser's Favorites section.

I believe this would make things a little bit easier. You just click a button on the page and BAM! you can view any submissions made by that author since the time at which you decided to add them to your Watch list.

Here's a preview of what it might look like:


The button would alternatively say "Remove Author" and that would remove the author from your Watch list.
----------


Underneath "My Maps" would go "My Authors" or "Watching..." or something, and this would be where all the submission of your favorite authors would be posted for you to view easily.


I would love to hear anyone's thoughts on this idea.

#19713 1 2008-03-28T07:05:12Z southpaw

Hello, everyone, and welcome to Portfolio, an image contest that has been drafted and will be maintained by southpaw.

You might be thinking how this contest differs from other image contests from the past year or so. In this contest you are not making only signatures. There will be much more of an emphasis on design and quality of multiple image styles rather than focusing on making sig images or editing pictures. Here you will be making a collection of images ranging from sigbars to advertisements. The idea of Portfolio is to develop your imaging skills by making a large set of images with some guidelines and rules.
Spoiler: Week 1Image for Week 1 is due by 11:59:59 PM (PST), Monday, April 7th, 2008

This week we will start out with something small to get us all warmed up. Not all of us have been constantly making images *glances at T3chno* so we'll take this week to get our feet wet.

Your first assignment is to create a signature that represents something personal and important. For example, if you love martial arts, or anime or Sharpies, then make a sig about it. If your dog has always been a close friend of yours then by all means incorporate him/her in there. If you love alcohol by all means, make a sig focused around alcohol. There are no limits.*

Requirements for Week 1:
  • Your sig must incorporate no more than 1 (one) thing that is personal and meaningful to you.
  • Sig size requirements must not exceed 600 pixels wide by 200 pixels tall and shall not be smaller than 100 pixels wide by 100 pixels tall.
Please PM me the final results, so as not to clutter up this thread. I'll be saving all of your images in your own seperate folders on my computer for your final Portfolio.

Good luck,
-southpaw-

*note: Please drink responsibly
Spoiler: Week 2Image for Week 2 is due by 11:59:59 (PST), Monday, April 14, 2008.

Welcome to Week 2! Glad to see the lot of you get in your images. Last week was great and I hope that this week turns out the same level, if not better, of quality.

This week we'll be focusing on music and album art. Your challenge for Week 2 is to create an album cover for your favorite band. For example, if you liked Hybrid Theory but didn't like the album art, redesign it. Or if you like Linkin Park in general you can come up with an original album art and put on a CD name that you think is fitting.

Requirements for Week 2:
  • Your album art must have the name of the artist and the name of the CD somewhere in a font that is legible. This means it can be fairly small but I must be able to read what the album name is and the artist name.
  • Your image cannot be larger than 12 centimeters (cm) wide by 12 cm tall.
  • You can create art for a fictional album and/or a fictional band, or you can recreate the album art of an album you like or enjoy.
Good luck to you all,
-southpaw-
Spoiler: Week 3Image for Week 3 will be due by 11:59:59 PM (PST), Monday, April 21st, 2008.

Welcome to Week 3 of Portfolio. For those of you that managed to complete your images for Week 2, congratulations. There was a wide range of style and design that I enjoyed looking at each and every one of the images that were PM'd or posted here in the thread.

Moving toward a more design aspect of the competition, this week we will be designing images using a stock image, which I have linked at the end of the post.

Logotypes (otherwise known as a logo) are designs that are intended to target a specific audience and/or get your attention toward a certain product. This week we will be designing an advertisement using a stock image.

Requirements for Week 3:
  • You must use one of the images in your advertisement.
  • You may only use ONE (1) of the logo's given in your advertisement.
  • Try to target a specific emotion or idea in your image with the intent of catching the attention of a certain audience (the targeted audience is completely up to you).
  • Your image may not be over 150 pixels/inch and must be no bigger than 6 inches wide by 4 inches tall.
Nokia
Lucky Strike

Hopefully you all can find some way to implement them into an advertisement. Can't wait and see what you all come up with!

-southpaw-
Spoiler: Week 4, Part 1Images for Week 4 will be due by the end of the contest. When it is your turn I will PM you to let you know. Your task is to get it all done while completing the remaining weeks. Week 4 will also be in two parts.

The challenge beginning here at Week 4 will be to construct our very own Image Worm. I am hoping to start off the Image worm for you all so that you may continue to work on it until the end of the competition. This will be a requirement for your Portfolio and may end up costing you many more votes if you cannot complete your portion.

I will be starting the image worm, at which point I will PM a contestant and ask them if they are willing to continue with the next part. Plan your time and find out when it would be best for you to work on an image for the worm. I'll gladly take requests for next in line, but for now I'll be PM'ing random members.

Requirements for Week 4:
  • Your image must be 640 pixels wide by 480 pixels tall, at 72 pixels/inch.
  • Blend from the previous image to the best of your ability.
This portion will continue until everyone has completed an image for the Image Worm. This will be considered a Contest Challenge, and is only the first part of Week 4's images.
Spoiler: Week 4, Part 2Images for Week 4, Part 2, will be due by Monday, May 5th, 2008 at 11:59:59 PM (PST)

This week's image will be given an extra week to work on so that we can all spend our best efforts on it. Emotions and personality is an important aspect to convey when doing certain things. Writing that does not have emotion or some flare of the writer's personality seems to lack quality at times. For the next couple weeks we'll be trying to convey emotions and personality in our images. I have created a list of emotions and matched them up with different people. This is your emotion that you must convey and cannot change it unless the person who you would like to change with doesn't mind taking your emotion.

Requirements for Week 4, Part 2:
  • There are no requirements other than conveying the emotion you are assigned.

Spoiler: Week 5Image for Week 5 will be due in 1 week, by Tuesday, May 13th, 2008.

Welcome to Week 5! Sorry to all contestants for the delay. Recently a few things have come up in my everyday life that I couldn't get to this until they were dealt with. I'm hoping that I can finish out this contest before anything else happens to come up also.

This week will be fairly simple and quite easy to do. Photo Manipulation is the task of changing the way a person perceives an image. Below is an example of such a task:

Original Image
Manipulated

Requirements for Week 5:
  • You must include the image you are manipulating in your entry so that I may see that it is an actual picture.
  • Brushes, vectors, renders, C4D's and the like should be kept to a minimum usage but I'm not excluding them for use.
good luck!
-southpaw-
Spoiler: Everything you wanted to know about the contest------------
A quick thanks to incluye for helping me clean up the description of the rules
Rules and Procedures of Portfolio:
  • • Each image must be ORIGINAL. This means that you CANNOT submit an image that you have already made.• Try and push your comfort zone when making the images but also feel that you did your best job.• Each image MUST meet its requirements. If I ask you to make a wallpaper with an orange bicycle in it, it has to have an orange bicycle in it. If I give size requirements it is expected that you follow those as well.• If I think that you haven't fulfilled the requirements, you have one extra day to finish the image. This does not mean that you can just turn your image in a day late. If you don't turn in your image in time, it will not be considered.• Nobody will be eliminated. This is not an elimination contest, rather it is a challenge amongst everyone.• The contest will run for 8 weeks. Each week there will be something due, so by the end of the contest you will hopefully have made at least 8 images fulfilling all the requirements of each week.• Each week will end on a Monday allowing time over the weekend to complete anything that one may be missing.• I will post the requirements for the following few weeks to give each person enough time to complete every image required. I would like each image and each week to become progressively harder to complete, meaning more time would be required to complete the image. The due dates will be set, but if you finish your image a week ahead of the due date I will accept it.• You may post your work elsewhere before submission so as to get feedback on it, but once you have officially submitted it there can be no other changes unless I feel it has not met the requirements.• Once all the images have been completed and the contest portion is over I will compile each persons images into a single portfolio, one for each contestant. From here there will be a public vote on which contestant's Portfolio is the best of the bunch.• The voting will be held for 1 single week. The person with the most votes at the end of that week will be the Portfolio Champion and will earn their spot within the community as a prestigious image maker.• If you managed to have missed a week without notifying me and getting permission to finish it later then I will be removing 1 vote per image that is not turned in.

Spoiler: The Chasm of Rain and ConclusionsAnd so there I stood, watching the raindrops fall,
at a puddle below me, while chaos surrounded all,
deep in a chasm they fell unknowingly,
from high up above the raindrops were falling.

And so I thought, from the depths of my being,
those raindrops are falling as though they had meaning,
that cause and effect have shown them to land,
in a pattern in that puddle beneath me down there.

This time was not silent, and often was broken,
but yelling cannot disturb my thoughts gone unspoken.
They are my own and belong to nobody else,
whether I share them or not is my choice alone.

But she wants to understand me, to completely know,
and I feel theres friction that will one day explode,
until piece by piece Im putting myself together and wonder,
"When did this whole thing get too out of hand?"

If its my fault then I hope I realize my part of the blame,
But if it comes down to this I wont live in shame,
I feel that something more important awaits me,
beyond the horizon, it always will bait me.

Kind of a continuation of Shadows of Light.

Quote: Strife, 2008-04-20T00:17:31Z
Why do you expect that the rules of addition or equality won't change? Because they are defined that way? What makes you think that the meaning of a mathematical definition won't change? Because we presume it to be permanent? Why do you expect that the concept of permanence will remain unchanged?

Because they are defined that way. Yes. The definitions can change, but the definitions are true by convention - mathematicians and like make all the definitions up, and then agree on which ones to adhere to. The conventions decide which meanings are to be used in a given situation. The meanings are arbitrary, but not unpredictable, and if they change, then the person using the rule must acknowledge the change, otherwise the change is not actually occurring.

Mathematical statements follow the same rules every time because we (loosely - humans, anyway) invented numbers and the rules that they follow, and those rules do not change unless we make them change.

I presume that the meanings won't change because we control whether or not they change.

Demonz, humans didn't invent numbers, they gave definition to numbers. One apple has always been one apple, but we defined the number one so that we may all know what we are talking about. We could have easily called it "gor apple" and it would have had the same meaning, just a different term. In essence we have created a system for defining amounts and portions in a way that most humans can understand such that communication becomes easier.

Strife, I guess it's hard to argue with someone who is taking the side against induction (or at least that's what I'm inferring from your post), but I'll assume that when you wake up in the morning you expect the sun to rise and that when you eat breakfast it will calm any hunger you may have, or at least stave it off until you can find something more substantial. The only thing I can say that would have any bearing it seems is that if the sun didn't rise the next day, or food didn't satisfy your hunger that you would have to adapt to this new change. Eventually you may realize that the sun is never rising again and that hunger is something you're just going to have to get used to. And so you adapt and readjust your reasoning for why things are the way they are. Though they may not have any real basis at least your point was proved that induction is not a great thing to live by because it causes one to assume things that may change dramatically in a short period of time.

So does this mean that induction is also a form of adaptation? To me it seems that this would be a valid point to bring up. We as humans, and other animals of many sorts, adapt to our environments based on our reasoning of what is the best way to survive. After a while the best way to survive is based on past experiences of what works and what doesn't. Our reasons for why we do things starts to become, "Because that is what has worked for me in the past." An example would be someone who is living in a forest would set up a shelter and start a campfire to stay warm because they reason that the fire will warm them up, as it has always done in the past.

Anyway, it just came to me that it could be possible. bah, someone pick this apart.

Quote: mattk210, April 26, 2008 04:11 pm
there is a dog that is getting into my back yard all the time and leaving poop all over the place.
Anyone have any idea how to get rid of the thing?

Land mines.

Really though, I checked around and found a few things about some laws that were passed in Australia about such things. If the dog belongs to someone and you know the person it belongs to, check out this website: http://www.tams.act.gov.au/.../dogdroppings

Quote: http://www.tams.act.gov.au/live/pets/dgctfactsht/dogdroppings
Will I receive a fine if I don't pick up my dog's droppings?

Yes. You can be fined for not picking up and disposing of your dogs droppings. On-the-spot fines of $50.00 can be issued by authorising officers. In addition, you can also receive an on-the-spot fine if you are not carrying appropriate equipment to collect your dog's droppings. The fine for not carrying collection equipment is $50.00.

So there you have it. Prove that the dog and the droppings are of the same and you can fine the person who owns the dog up to $50.00 AUD. That'd probably be enough to let them get the message to have tighter control of their dog. This may only work when walking your dog but it could be worth a shot.

Also, I was looking around that site a little more and it looks like there are a lot of domestic animal laws, which I didn't find surprising, but was a little amazed at how many there were. Fairly strict policies, some.

Here's another resource that I found: http://www.tams.act.gov.au/.../dogwelfare-codeofpractice.pdf
Quote: http://www.tams.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0016/13642/dogwelfare-codeofpractice.pdf
2.1 General
The owner of a dog must provide for its physical, emotional and behavioural
needs. Dogs must be under the control of the owner at all times. Humans and
other animals, such as other dogs, cats, wildlife and farm animals, may be
affected or endangered by uncontrolled dog behaviour. Owners should take
reasonable precautions to prevent escape of a dog from their premises or
vehicle. Dogs should be securely confined within the property boundary.
Invisible fences are not permitted under the Act.

Either way you have enough proof to at least fine the owner(s) of the dog I think. I hope this clears up some mystery of the domestic animal laws in Australia. I don't know if you live in Canberra but if you did the website from which I found this information was for Canberra... so I guess it would apply to Canberra residents more than anyone else.

#20206 1 2008-05-11T11:53:35Z southpaw
I think we can all mostly agree that with a rating system that uses averages it is easy to throw the rating of a map with just a few votes, regardless of the quality of the map. It also means that one doesn't have to play the map to make a fair judgment, which is where snipers come into play.

Now, there have been quite a few attempts at changing the voting system to get rid of snipers, and for the most part they have been good ideas but with many flaws. I think this is mostly because some people have created systems which are far too simple that it isn't really rating a map anymore, or they become far too complex because the person has many ideas that -could- stop sniping, but the sheer amount of ideas put together make the system too complex and in the end there are many flaws.

I think I have found a voting system that takes power away from a sniper and still allows a top rated system that will almost be completely unchanged.

To start, let's imagine that instead of using a rating system that averages scores let us use a rating system that adds scores. Let me explain a little more. Averaging the score of a map puts power into those who want to abuse a system that decreases the "value" of a map. For example, someone rates a map a 4 and another person rates the map a 0. the average score for the map is now 2, when it could easily be a 3.5 or 4. This means someone has just decreased the "value" of that map by rating it low.

With this new system, rating a 0 is not of importance, because it would essentially be a No Rate (NR). Instead of averaging the scores I suggest that we add the scores. If a person rates a map a 5 and another person rates the map a 2 the score will be 7. this means you can only add to the value of a players map, rather than decrease the value of a players map.

so the options are as follows: 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5. All maps in this new voting system will be rated and compared to all other maps in terms of total score rather than average score. this kind of comparison is just as good and just as effective. The higher your score overall the higher it is on the rating scale. This is how the current system works, and this is how this new system works.

Now, on to the Top Rated page, because that's where this kind of cuts out the benefit of having an average rating. But I have a solution. Top Rated will have a minimum standard that will automatically put a map up there if it has received at least a score of 23 in its first five votes (that's two +4's and three +5's). Then the Top Rated page will also be ordered by date that they were added to the page, rather than average rating. I would say that as long as a map has made it to the Top Rated page it should stay there indefinitely. This means that the Top Rated page could cycle through new maps all the time and let people see what is new and fresh and great rather than AfternoonDragonStep04 on the front page always.

I'm very tired as of now but I wanted to get this up and see what people thought of it. I'm sorry if this idea has been thought of before, I'm just too lazy to search for the same idea...

I'll explain in more detail, possibly with picture, if people would like me to.

Yes, but that doesn't mean that God ordained this flood. It simply means that a flood came through the Middle East a long long time ago.

Quote: wikipedia
The Akkadian Atrahasis Epic (written no later than 1700 BC, the name Atrahasis means "exceedingly wise"), gives human overpopulation as the cause for the great flood. After 1200 years of human fertility, the god Enlil felt disturbed in his sleep due to the noise and ruckus caused by the growing population of mankind. He turned for help to the divine assembly who then sent a plague, then a drought, then a famine, and then saline soil, all in an attempt to reduce the numbers of mankind. All these were temporary fixes. 1200 years after each solution, the original problem returned. When the gods decided on a final solution, to send a flood, the god Enki, who had a moral objection to this solution, disclosed the plan to Atrahasis, who then built a survival vessel according to divinely given measurements.

Sound a little familiar? You see, the reason your flood story has been proven to be true is because many other religions also recorded this great flood. And chances are some large boat or seafaring vessel was built that carried many people. There is no proof that God ordained this. In fact here it says that the god Enlil caused the flood, not your Christian God.

From what I have read (which isn't much, but this is what I have taken from it so far) the Bible is both a story about morals AND a history of the ancient world. [qutoe=SkyRay]I am missing the top rated, but i think it should be RECENT top rated, so we don't always see the afternoon dragon step 04, up at #1 half the time. Just great top rated maps in the past few days or so would be great.[/quote]
I believe that this is how the Hottest Maps section works. Every vote that increases a maps rating pushes it higher up on the list and every vote that decreases its rating pushes it lower down on the list. It takes the highest rated map of most recently and shifts it to the top. Any map that is just submitted will be shoved to the top of the list, because 0 out of 0 is probably the "highest" rating anybody can get. Maps with disabled ratings are put at the top of the list when they are submitted but will be pushed down lower and lower as new maps are pushed higher and higher and as new maps are submitted.

I think there is a time limit that maps are on the Hottest Maps page as well, so that way the highest rated maps overall since the redesign don't stay up there indefinitely.

#447110 6 2008-06-21T17:48:38Z southpaw
I have talked with Arachnid about this and he has a plan like this in the works.

From what he told me it will be known as a 'token-bucket' system. What this means is that for every map a person posts a 'token' is taken away from their stock of tokens. At the most a person can accrue 3 token. You earn tokens back through time, so 1 token may be received every hour, or every 3 hours, or however long Arachnid would like (he was saying one hour but I think that was just an example).

It was suggested that this system could also be set manually for certain users who are abusing their privileges on NUMA, so by setting their token maximum to 0 they are essentially banned from submitting maps until a certain date. #447163 65 2008-06-21T21:10:25Z southpaw
Quote: Strife, June 21, 2008 12:05 pm
Quote: southpaw, 2008-06-21T08:59:56Z
God is subjective.
Beauty is subjective. Humor is subjective. Subjectivity only applies to things that are defined entirely by opinion. The existence of God is not such a thing; He either exists or doesn't, just like a table can either exist or not (and a table, if you didn't catch it, is not subjective).
The importance of faith is subjective. God is not subjective.

I disagree.

Things can only be objective if there is observable data that can be viewed. You wouldn't say that a table has 4 legs and is in a rectangular shape without some kind of observable data to prove your point to others. What if someone had only seen round tables their entire life? How would you prove to them that some tables do in fact have 4 legs? You would need objective data to show them that other types of tables exist.

Same thing happens with a God. There is no objective data that we can accurately say was the work of a God. Religion is speculating and believing that there is a God, but without objective data there is no proof that God is omnibenevolent, omnipotent, or that He even exists.
---
But in light of my discussion here, let me rephrase my statement. God is objective. The properties of God are subjective. It is up to the person, and not through objective data, whether or not God sends people to Hell, if he is truly omnibenevolent, if he created man in His own image, whose side God is on during a religious war, if God allows you to kill those who do not believe in Him the same way you do, etc etc etc

These are all subjective properties of God, for they are made up in the mind of individuals and can be changed depending on a person's ideals from one time to another. The nice thing about a God that has no objective proof is that his properties can become subjective. This is why I said God is subjective.
Unless you believe God is everything, in which case you can walk outside and view God in all of God's glory. Still, you can make up your mind about what God's glory is and in that case God is still subjective.

#448480 19 2008-06-25T08:19:46Z southpaw
Quote: TribulatioN, June 24, 2008 06:52 pm
The Top Rated should be tweaked so that it starts showing just the top rated action maps? Or something of that sort.

Top Rated should only come back under a couple of conditions:

If you were to bring back Top Authors, there should be 5 levels of top rated authors, with each level weighted differently.
  • Level 1 : This would belong to the top authors around on NUMA. Maps in this category would belong to authors with 60+ rated maps. This would show who has been the most dedicated to NUMA and who has the most amount of highest rated maps.
  • Level 2 : This would belong to authors with greater than 30 rated maps, but less than 60 rated maps. This would show up-and-coming authors that are getting recognition in the community for their awesome maps.
  • Level 3 : This would belong to authors with greater than 15 rated maps but less than 30 rated maps. It would be for newcomers to earn a recognition spot.
  • Level 4 : This would belong to those with less than 15 rated maps and would essentially be where n00bs start out at. There wouldn't be much recognition here, but it would be a place that some people could browse if they wanted to see who was coming up through the ranks as far as n00bs go.
  • Level 5 : The lowest level would belong to the authors who have disabled ratings. It would be weighted by how many times their maps have been favourited (I know it's a little sketch but it's the only thing I can think of to weight it by). This would essentially be a separate section to see which authors don't want their maps rated but still want the recognition.
This would have to be the only way I would think for Top Authors to come back. Otherwise you'll have Clifty, who is far from the best map maker on NUMA, at the top of the list again and it'd be stupid.

---

As for Top Rated, I think a similar system would have to occur, but ratings should have heavier weight to get to the Top Rated page. In the old system you needed just three 5's and two 4.5's to get a map on the Top Rated page. In any new Top Rated system I would like to see 2 things.
  • 1.) Maps are ordered by the date at which they became Top Rated. Otherwise you'll have Afternoon Dragon sitting at the top of the charts again. I think Top Rated maps should be ordered by the day at which they were put on the list, not by their ratings. In this way the Top Rated page would stay looking fresh and you wouldn't see the same maps over and over again.
  • 2.) Ratings for Top Rated should be weighted more. Increase the number of rates to reach Top Rated to 10 or 15 votes. Any map with an average rating of 4.8 or over after so many votes would get a spot on the Top Rated page.
If these things were not added to the Top Rated and Top Authors list, I probably wouldn't support their return unless somebody had an amazingly convincing argument otherwise.

This thread is not meant to advertise for yourself but rather bring attention to others. Therefore I will stop accepting posts from new authors who would like to be noticed and only accept posts from authors who I trust can make good decisions about great new authors.

For those new authors who would like to gain some attention, please use either:
The Map-Rating Thread
-OR-
The Map Commenting Thread
Then if you feel like you would like some notice, suggest to somebody who is well know if they would consider referring you to this page, at which point I'll take a look and decide if I agree and from there you will be added. #20752 1 2008-07-09T09:22:21Z southpaw
I think it's time for another recipe thread. Food is something that I think I can say we all enjoy. This thread is meant to share your favorite recipes with the rest of the community. I encourage some of you to go ahead and try them and let us know how well it went! Even if you can't cook well, maybe you could ask someone, such as a parent or a friend, to do the cooking for you.

I guess I'll start with a couple of my favorite recipes:
Spoiler: [bAfrican Chicken Peanut Soup[/b]]
===========================

INGREDIENTS:
---
2 tablespoons olive oil
1 clove of garlic, crushed
1/2 yellow onion, finely diced
1 large carrot, grated
1 sweet red pepper, thinly sliced
1/3 cup tomato paste
2/3 cup creamy peanut butter (NOT natural or 'old-fashoined')
1/2 teaspoon cayenne
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
4 cups chicken broth
1 1/2 - 2 cups shredded cooked chicken

===========================

PROCEDURE:
---
1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and add garlic, onion, carrot and red pepper. Simmer until onion is transparent.
2. Stir in tomato paste until it is evenly absorbed. Once it is absorbed, stir in the peanut butter and stir until the peanut butter is absorbed into the vegetable mixture.
3. Add the cayenne, salt, and black pepper, then gradually stir in the chicken broth, 1 cup at a time.
4. When the broth has emulsified with the vegetable-peanut butter mixture, add shredded chicken.
5. Simmer for 15 minutes (I simmer it uncovered). More salt or cayenne may be added for taste.

===========================

RECOMMENDATIONS:
---
1. Before heating any pans or starting any cooking, get all of your ingredients chopped, diced, sliced, grated, shredded, etc. It's difficult to cook this meal if you don't have everything prepared as stated.

2. I like to use crunchy Jif peanut butter. The little peanut kernels are great for texture and Jif tastes delicious. If you don't have crunchy Jif peanut butter then use the best tasting peanut butter you know of that fits the requirements.

3. If you can, buy a pre-cooked chicken. It's less work because you don't have to cook the chicken yourself, and pre-cooked chickens from the store usually taste pretty good. Don't use the skin though, I just eat that as I shred the chicken.

4. Although the recipe says to do everything in a saucepan, I like to cook the vegetable mixture in the saucepan only. When you get to the part where you have to add tomato paste I transfer the vegetable mixture to a heated soup pot, then add the tomato paste once I have the vegetables in the pot. From there it's really easy because you don't have to worry about overflowing the saucepan once you start pouring the chicken broth in.

5. Make a double batch! This soup tastes 4 times better after 24 hours, and making a double batch allows a lot of leftovers.

===========================
Spoiler: [bsouthpaw's Cinnamon Milkshake[/b]]
===========================

INGREDIENTS:
Vanilla Ice Cream
Milk
Cinnamon
Almond flavoring (NOT organic, the kind that has alcohol in it)

===========================

PROCEDURE:
This is my own creation, so I haven't taken exact measurements, but I will approximate what I have used.

1. Make 2 cups of a regular milkshake with the vanilla ice cream and milk. If you can make this in a large mug with a fairly wide mouth that would be perfect.

2. Coat the top of the milkshake with cinnamon (about 2 teaspoons). Stir until the cinnamon starts clumping together in little specks in the milkshake.

3. 1/8 ounce Almond flavoring. Stir until you feel it has been mixed in thoroughly. Enjoy!

===========================

RECOMMENDATIONS:

1. If there is too much almond flavor, or not enough cinnamon just experiment with measurements until you get it just right! This may take anywhere from the second try or the 7th try, but it's worth it once you have figured out how much of each you like in your milkshake.

===========================


Now, let's hear some of YOUR recipes!

I'm proposing a compromise in light of the very few but very adamant people who think that Nreality and NUMA should not be associated with each other.

As of now, when you click the Maps tab in the navigation bar on NUMA you get the following tag options:
+playable +action +puzzle +race +dda +n-art

Here's my idea:

+playable +action +puzzle +race +dda +tileset +n-art +nreality +imagemap
-playable -action -puzzle -race -dda -tileset -n-art -nreality -imagemap

As you can see, it would include BOTH tags for the more common tags. People would then be able to view common map types without having to type in the map type in the search box. People could include the maps types they want and do not want to see.

As far as I'm concerned, checkboxes are a bad idea.

It used to be that you had to choose what type of map (action, puzzle, survival, DDA, etc.) your submission was before you could continue. When I first started out on NUMA, that was confusing to me. I had no idea what an action map or a puzzle map or a race map should look and play like, so I had no idea what to choose.

If anything, Nreality tags, if added automatically, should be added via basic code at the end of the map. Or for imagemaps, maybe a check on the URL so as to make sure that it is a valid URL. I don't know how hard these would be, but for those just beginning N and NUMA there shouldn't be something that they can choose for themselves. Rather Nreality should be something that is a part of NUMA, but not to the extent that anybody could check a little Nreality checkbox when they have no idea what Nreality is.

Code recognition and URL verification is the best way to ensure that all player/drone mods and image maps are accounted for. As far as difficulty in the coding process, I have no idea how hard it would be. But to me this seems like the best way to prevent abuse of people checking the Nreality checkbox (such as those trying to make statements about Nreality and NUMA) but allows Nreality maps to be easily found with the tag suggestion from the first post.

southpaw's take on the issue:

I think that there are some things that need to be cleared up. Not all of the current Reviewers on NUMA are the best with words. Some even write at a grade 5 reading level, which just doesn't cut it for me.

If Bitesizing were to come back there are two things I would hope to make clear:
  • Bitesizer's should NOT be Reviewer's, and vice versa.
  • Featured maps should not be able to be bitesized, but bitesized maps should be allowed to be featured.
Bitesizer's and reviewers should be separate because there are people who have a keen sense of what a great map is that should have the ability to show everyone else, even though their choices of words may not be stellar. This is where Reviewer's come in. They should only be able to show the maps that they think are the cream of the crop and be able to eloquently explain why they think so. This is also why I think the Reviewer's section needs to be cleaned up. Not all the reviewer's have a great choice of words and would be much better suited having essentially the same position but without having to pen the reasons for their decision.

As for Featured maps not able to be bitesized, I think that this is fair. If Featured Maps are supposed to be the best of the best, and bitesized maps are supposed to be a map that is implemented amazingly well (even if it does have 1 or 2 flaws) then there should be no reason why Featured maps should HAVE to be bitesized. Featured maps are already amazing. Bitesized maps just have to be maps that play well.

Also, while typing this post I came across the idea that possiby reviewer's should have to post a review every 2 months or have to reapply for Reviewership. This way only those who really have something to say should be given the status, otherwise it's wasted on individuals. Why have something if you're not going to use it?
